steps.what: Observe, feel, taste or otherwise examine products during and after processing

tasks.design: Keep sensory and physical product examination with the operator. Standards in {DOCS} support assessment without supplying an automatic product-conformance decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Texture, appearance and other product characteristics require actual examination.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital standards can be referenced, but no validated replacement for this examination is provided.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle changes and conflicting sensory indicators need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognizes meaningful differences in the actual product.
tasks.altitude: Examination time and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Relating sensory changes to processing conditions

evidence.claim: Physical and sensory examination remains human work without a validated task-specific sensing replacement.

assumptions: Boundary is examination against standards, excluding separate production records and downstream quality release.
The operator produces conformance assessment during s1. No structured acceptable-product flag is assumed before examination.
Use native standard-document access before custom tools. No new sensing or record capture is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the task is unchanged.
research_questions: Which conformance characteristics require sensory judgement rather than existing instrument readings?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Consistent batches and borderline samples both retain physical examination.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe conditions and adjust process controls

steps.what: Observe temperature, humidity, pressure gauges and product samples against prescribed conditions
Check the required adjustment and adjust thermostats or valves for the processing stage

tasks.design: Retain observation and control adjustment with the operator. Existing control functions in {OTHER} may already regulate set points, and their runtime earns no new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: The operator relates instrument readings and product condition to the actual processing stage.
tasks.enabler_now: Native machine controls provide established regulation, but no new validated control change is specified here.
tasks.still_hard: Instrument anomalies and product response require contextual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognizes when nominal readings do not match the product.
tasks.altitude: Operating responsibility and task time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Relate product development to processing conditions
reach.learn: Recognizing product response to temperature and moisture

evidence.claim: Existing automatic regulation does not establish an additional saving in the operator's remaining observation and adjustment work.

assumptions: Boundary covers remaining human observation and adjustments, excluding existing automatic regulation and separately counted production record entry.
The operator produces assessed operating condition in s1 and checks an adjustment in s2. No ready-made verified stage, sensor-validity or safe-adjustment flag is assumed.
OTHER denotes machine control equipment. Test native functions before custom code; no new control automation is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because hardware, controls and workflow remain unchanged.
unknowns: Existing automatic regulation and permitted operator adjustments
research_questions: Is any remaining adjustment fully specified by verified inputs, without requiring product judgement?

already_counted.description: Adjustment check and operation of controls

approvals.approved_version: Exact machine, processing stage, observed condition and proposed control setting checked before adjustment in s2; changed conditions require another check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Normal operation and abnormal product response both retain observation and checked adjustment.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch material flow and report unresolved malfunctions

steps.what: Observe material flow, listen for malfunctions and perform permitted corrective actions
Notify supervisors when corrective actions fail to resolve the observed malfunction

tasks.design: Keep direct observation, permitted corrective work and escalation with the operator. Existing equipment information in {OTHER} may support the response without assuming reliable automated detection of every jam or spill.
tasks.previous_blocker: Malfunctions are identified through the actual behavior and sound of equipment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing equipment alarms support some conditions but do not establish complete detection or resolution.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual sounds and failed corrections require judgement and clear escalation.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognizes abnormal behavior and explains what happened and what was attempted.
tasks.altitude: Observation, correction and escalation remain unchanged.

reach.task: Recognize processing equipment problems affecting product condition
reach.learn: Clear communication of symptoms and attempted corrections

evidence.claim: Human observation and response cannot be removed by assuming every malfunction already has a reliable structured alarm.

assumptions: Boundary is operator observation, permitted first response and notification, excluding supervisory decisions and specialist repair.
The operator produces observed malfunction status and corrective action outcome in s1 before notifying in s2. No structured unresolved-fault code exists for free.
OTHER denotes machine control equipment. Review native alarms before custom tools; this design adds no automated fault detection or escalation.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new system or data capture is introduced. Supervisor and repair effort remain outside the focal-role denominator.
unknowns: Existing alarms and allowed operator corrections
research_questions: Are any existing alarms demonstrably reliable enough to reduce a separately measured monitoring burden?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Easily corrected interruptions and unresolved malfunctions retain observation, response and communication.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Capture product identity, weight, quantity, processing time and temperature from the actual batch
Record the captured production values in the production register
Check production records against readings, resolve discrepancies and accept the record

tasks.design: Configure native production forms in {OPS_SYSTEM} so one operator capture produces the record draft. The operator checks batch identity, measurements and corrections before accepting it; instruments are not assumed to supply a verified feed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were copied from batch observations into a separate register.
tasks.enabler_now: A native form can save entered fields directly and populate the record without retyping.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong batch selection, missing readings and questionable measurements need operator verification.
tasks.human_edge: The operator checks that recorded values describe the actual processing event.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated transcription leaves measurement and record acceptance with the operator.

reach.learn: Clear batch identification and traceable corrections

evidence.claim: A native production form can save captured fields and eliminate repeat transcription; this processing-record design and saving are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is recording production data, excluding performing measurements already needed for control and sensory product examination. Capture here counts linking and entering the observed values, without duplicating physical observation time in other tasks.

The processing machine operator produces in s1 batch identifier, product type, weight and unit, quantity and unit, processing stage, observed timestamp or duration and unit, temperature and unit, and reading source. Capture time remains fully counted; missing or unclear fields require manual correction before acceptance.
Test native OPS_SYSTEM forms and record views before custom code. No automatic instrument feed or structured discrepancy code is assumed; s3 identifies discrepancies from source readings.
Existing automatic records earn no saving. If values are already captured once, there is no s2 transcription baseline to remove.
unknowns: Existing paper register and duplicate entry
Access requirements and national employee consultation needs for timestamped records
research_questions: Does single capture remove repeat entry after counting field capture, record checks and form upkeep?

already_counted.description: Source comparison, discrepancy resolution and record acceptance

incremental.description: Maintain form fields and handle recording exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact batch, product, values, units, timestamps and correction history checked before acceptance in s3; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R60 gross40 minus8 upkeep gives net32. Range0-7 assumes substantial existing single capture or limited repeated transcription; physical observation and acceptance retain time.

reach: Learn traceable batch corrections from butchers
Relate process observations to product condition with bakers
